report.verdict: Revenue grew +3%, but Flutter swung to a $296m net loss with adjusted EBITDA halving (-45%). Critically, the entire 2026 revenue and EBITDA downgrade came from FanDuel (US) — International guidance is unchanged. This is a deliberate trough year: the UK's 40% gaming-tax reset, heavy World Cup and Rewards-Club reinvestment, and unlucky US sports results compress margins before a 2027+ cost-savings and hold-normalisation recovery. The growth engine (US #1 positions, iGaming) is intact; shares still fell ~12%.
summary: **The downgrade is 100% FanDuel.** The 2026 revenue and EBITDA cut came entirely from the US; International guidance is unchanged — a US-specific reinvestment/hold story, not a group-wide deterioration.
**Group revenue +3% to $4,326m** but a GAAP net loss of $(296)m vs +$37m a year ago; adjusted EPS $0.49, below the ~$0.54 consensus, -83% YoY.
**Adj. EBITDA halved to $508m (-45%),** group margin -1,020bps to 11.7% — the number that defines the quarter.
**The World Cup was a genuine success.** Group World Cup revenue grew 164% on 2022 to more than $300m; handle topped $3bn (+174%) and actives exceeded 10m (+88%).
**US revenue -6% to $1.68bn** on customer-friendly sports results; International +10% to $2.64bn (+4% organic) carried the top line.
**Product mix: iGaming is the engine.** Group iGaming +9% to $1,935m; sportsbook broadly flat at $2,229m (-1%).
**UK duty is the structural shock:** remote gaming duty stepped up (to 40%), the main driver of the -19% fall in International EBITDA despite +10% revenue.

**Cost program ahead of schedule and expanding.** Ahead of the earlier $300m-by-2027 savings plan, with a further ~$200m of UK-tax mitigation also expected in 2027; a new 'Phase 2' targets an additional $500m of gross opex + capex savings by 2029.

**Guidance cut, all in the US:** group revenue midpoint -$395m to $17.91bn; adj. EBITDA midpoint -$210m to $2.655bn. The revenue cut includes a $75m hit from a one-week NFL-season delay ($50m to EBITDA).
**US H2 is heavily back-end loaded:** US adj. EBITDA was $119m in Q2 (H1 $238m); management expects Q3 ~break-even, implying Q4 must exceed $500m to hit the $760m FY US EBITDA midpoint.

**Deliberate generosity step-up:** US promo is guided to ~6% of handle in H2 (from 5.4% in Q2) as the new Rewards Club reaches 100% of the base for the NFL season — near-term margin sacrifice to 'extend FanDuel's leading position.'

**Prediction markets scaling as an incremental leg:** FanDuel Predicts made $6m of trading revenue in Q2 and is expected to generate ~$50m this year; 'limited cannibalization' of regulated OSB, with a 'One App' and Crypto-exchange integration landing before NFL.
**Balance sheet stretched but cash-generative:** net debt $10,480m, leverage 4.3x; operating cash flow $363m (+1%), free cash flow $189m (+21%). No buyback — cash to de-leveraging.
**CEO transition:** Peter Jackson steps down after 9 years; Dan Taylor becomes CEO on 1 Oct 2026 — a handover into a reinvestment year.
**Early Q3 trading is ahead of expectations,** helped by World Cup knockout engagement and 'slightly favourable' sports results.

**Thesis read-through:** #1 US positions and iGaming momentum are intact; 2026 is a trough year (UK tax + US reinvestment + World Cup) before a 2027+ recovery. The Q4-loaded US guide and promo escalation are the key risks.
**Market reaction:** shares fell ~11.8% to $92.56 on the day — the market is pricing the US profit hole and Q4 execution risk, not a broken thesis.

segments.name: US (FanDuel)
segments.headline: Demand is strong and #1 positions held; the miss is hold and deliberate reinvestment, not customers.
narrative: They retained their #1 positions in US online sports and iGaming, with GGR market shares of 39% and 27% respectively. Overall US revenue fell 6% to $1.68bn, with monthly actives 9% higher at 3.84m but ARPU 14% lower at $146, and they guided H2 market growth to remain subdued and consistent with H1 at mid-single-digit.

Marketing spend jumped 61% to $353m, or 21.0% of revenue, driven by the World Cup and FanDuel Predicts investment. Handle rose 2% to $12.0bn, but the net sports margin fell 1.7pp to 8.7%. The structural revenue margin actually improved 0.4pp to 14.0% on greater Same-Game-Parlay penetration during the World Cup; however, adverse results combined with promotional spend at 5.4% of handle cut sports net revenue 15% to $1.04bn, while sports actives grew 8% to 2.91m and ARPU fell 20% to $119.

Their Rewards Club programme now reaches 70% of the customer base and will hit 100% for the start of the NFL season. Feedback has been positive, but it will push promotional spend toward roughly 6% of handle in H2 — a proactive investment they expect to extend FanDuel's leading position. Early signals from the improvement plan are encouraging: NBA Finals handle was up 40% year-on-year with actives up 25%, and the World Cup drew 2.3m US actives, a third of them reactivated, which bodes well for the NFL season.

On prediction markets, FanDuel Predicts is positioned as incremental rather than cannibalistic. A crypto-exchange integration has improved the product ahead of the NFL season, a nationwide 'One App' is coming, and they report only limited cannibalization in regulated OSB states. They made $6m of trading revenue in Q2 and expect around $50m for the year, citing a market-making advantage.

iGaming revenue grew 14% to $577m, on 14% growth in iGaming actives to 1.04m and a 26% increase in direct-to-casino acquisition, supported by monthly exclusive releases — including Huff N' Puff and Willy Wonka titles — through year-end.

On guidance, the US now expects FY26 revenue of $7.4bn (down $395m) and adjusted EBITDA of $760m (down $210m) at the midpoints; the revenue cut includes a $75m hit from the one-week NFL-season delay ($50m to EBITDA). Q2 adjusted EBITDA fell 45% to $119m, taking H1 to $238m; with Q3 expected around break-even, Q4 EBITDA needs to exceed $500m to meet the guide.

segments.name: International
segments.headline: +10% revenue (guidance unchanged), but EBITDA -20% on UK tax and World Cup marketing; regional mix strong ex-Brazil.
narrative: Total revenue, which includes the various retail businesses, grew 10% to $2.64bn, or 4% organically. Adjusted EBITDA fell 20% to $486m (an 18.0% margin), the decline driven primarily by higher UK taxes and increased World Cup marketing — the latter up 19% to $446m, or 16.9% of revenue. Actives were 16% lower at 10.5m, mainly reflecting the closure of India last year. By product, reported sports revenue rose 14% to $1.19bn (+4% organic) and gaming rose 7% to $1.36bn (+3% organic).

UK & Ireland revenue increased 4% to $971m (+3% in local currency). iGaming was up 7% on a 22% rise in iGaming actives, helped by new exclusive content and the Flutter Jackpots rollout, and Sky Gaming has improved since the platform migration. Sportsbook revenue fell 2% on handle down 1%, though Sky Bet — down year-on-year for five straight quarters — was flat in Q2 and up 20% in June. They are executing their UK tax-mitigation plan and expect to take share as competitors react. Per the 10-Q, the UK alone was $882m (+4%) and Ireland $80m (+4%).

In Southern Europe & Africa, reported revenue rose 36% to $896m, or 18% excluding SNAI. In Italy, Sisal's proposition delivered a record market share in June and, with the benefit of the PokerStars migration, extended their #1 online position — 30.9% versus Lottomatica at 30.3%. The April SNAI migration was a success; after the expected May lull, SNAI actives grew 30% in June as customers gained access to Sisal's product.

Brazil revenue was up 64% as reported to $72m. Operational progress was offset by a slowdown in the online market driven by government socio-economic measures, including a centralised self-exclusion register; performance was broadly in line with the market, with actives 6% lower and organic revenue down 14%. In May they integrated Flutter's core product and pricing onto the Brazilian platform, which caused an initial dip in engagement before activity recovered, with BetBuilder bets up fivefold.

Asia-Pacific revenue was down 1% to $398m, of which Australia was $401m — up 12% as reported but only 1% in local currency (A$564m); turnover rose 12%, a positive sports performance offset by softness in greyhound racing, and World Cup actives grew 43% versus 2022. Central & Eastern Europe revenue rose 23% to $170m (+21% constant currency), with iGaming up 16% on product gains and share wins in Serbia, Georgia and Armenia, and sports turnover up 21% (cc) at a 3.1pp better net margin, lifting net sports revenue 59%.
Crucially, International's 2026 guidance is unchanged — the entire group downgrade sits with FanDuel.

highlights.text: US #1 positions held (OSB 39%, iGaming 27% GGR share) and demand strong — NBA Finals handle +40%, actives +25%; the miss is hold, not customers
US structural revenue margin +0.4pp to 14.0% on Same-Game-Parlay penetration — the durable margin lever
iGaming momentum broad-based: US +14% ($577m, actives +14%), UK iGaming actives +22%, CEE iGaming +16%
World Cup a clear success: group revenue >$300m (+164% vs 2022), handle >$3bn, actives >10m; a third of US World Cup actives reactivated
Italy #1 online extended (30.9% share) with a record June; SNAI migration delivering (+30% June actives)
Self-help credible and ahead of plan: $300m savings by 2027 + ~$200m UK mitigation + new $500m Phase 2 by 2029
FCF +21% to $189m even through the margin shock

lowlights.text: Group adj. EBITDA -45%, margin -1,020bps to 11.7% — the defining negative
US adj. EBITDA -70% to $119m (H1 $238m); Q3 guided ~break-even, so Q4 must exceed $500m — heavy back-end risk
US sports NGR -15% to $1.04bn on adverse results plus promo at 5.4% of handle, rising toward ~6% in H2
UK gaming-duty step-up is a permanent headwind; International EBITDA -20% despite +10% revenue
Marketing surged: US S&M +61% ($353m, 21% of revenue), International +19% ($446m) — partly event-led, partly ongoing Rewards Club
Brazil online slowdown on government socio-economic measures; organic revenue -14%
Guidance cut -$395m revenue / -$210m EBITDA (entirely US); shares -11.8% on the day

forecast.intro: The full downgrade sits with FanDuel; International guidance is unchanged. New US FY26 guidance is revenue $7.4bn (-$395m) and adj. EBITDA $760m (-$210m) at midpoints, including a $75m one-week NFL-delay revenue hit ($50m to EBITDA). Group FY26 midpoints move to $17.91bn revenue (-$395m) and $2.655bn adj. EBITDA (-$210m). With US Q2 EBITDA of $119m (H1 $238m) and Q3 guided ~break-even, Q4 US EBITDA must exceed $500m to hit the FY midpoint.
forecast.view: 2026 is a **trough margin year** and the risk is squarely H2-US-execution: the FY US EBITDA guide is Q4-loaded (>$500m in one quarter) just as promo steps to ~6% of handle for the Rewards Club rollout. I'd treat the group revenue midpoint ($17.91bn) as fair-to-slightly-full given subdued US market growth and Brazil headwinds, with International the reliable anchor (guidance unchanged, Italy/CEE strong). Group adj. EBITDA margin should recover off the 11.7% Q2 low as World Cup spend rolls off and Q4 NFL leverages the US base — but the quality of that recovery hinges on hold normalising rather than being bought with generosity. Leverage (4.3x) should ease toward ~3.5-4.0x on H2 cash; **no near-term buyback**. The 2027 setup is attractive if the $300m + ~$200m UK-mitigation savings land and prediction markets scale.
watch: US promo as % of handle (5.4% -> ~6%) and Rewards Club payback — reinvestment or a generosity spiral?
The Q4 US EBITDA >$500m dependency — early NFL trading and net sports margin are make-or-break.
UK share and Sky Bet trajectory post-duty (June +20%) — is the share-gain thesis real?
Brazil regulation and the post-integration recovery; International keeping its unchanged guide.
FanDuel Predicts ramp (One App, Crypto integration) and cannibalisation; and the de-leveraging path under new CEO Dan Taylor.
